newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya sees higher coffee sales in 1995/96.
newsitem.headline: Kenya sees higher coffee sales in 1995/96.

text.p: Kenyan coffee authorities on Tuesday reported higher sales in the first 10 months of 1995/96 compared with the same 1994/95 period and said this pointed to a better overall export performance this year.
But a weaker global market undermined earnings, they said.

"Since the beginning of the current coffee year, October to July 1995/96, a total of 1,461,422 60-kg bags of coffee with a realisation value of 12,335,093,300 shillings (FOB Mombasa) have been exported to all destinations," Coffee Board of Kenya Public Relations Manager Paul Kivila said.
"During the same period last year (1994/95), 989,165 bags valued at 10,744,439,660 shillings had been exported," Kivila said in a statement.

Kivila said that at end-July, a total of 42 auctions had been held with 1,699,285 bags of coffee sold. Total earnings from these sales amounted to $238,463,860, with an overall sale average of $116.94 per 50 kg bag.
That compared with 1,365,644 bags worth $276,360,164.54 over the same period in the previous year.
Coffee is measured in 60-kg bags but sold at Kenya's weekly export auction in Nairobi in units of 50 kg.
Kivila said the data indicated a steady rise in the quantity of coffee exported by Kenya, but earnings were lower in line with international market trends.
